A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same overlap-splitting study and ColorShapeDigit800K dataset. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title and expanded experimental scope.

before.justification: v1 reports original ResNet-18, VAE and nanoGPT experiments, including similarity measurements, classification accuracies, mutual information and generated samples in Section 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original similarity and model-performance experiments, plus adversarial-image and jailbreak-transfer results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices A.2–A.4.

M1.justification: The proposed dataset splitting and both task splitting procedures retain the same partition-selection and relabeling rules, including ColorShapeDigit800K. New model families, training configurations and downstream attacks extend the experiments without changing these proposed procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds adversarial-image transfer on TinyImageNet and jailbreak-transfer evaluation using harmful requests from AdvBench. CIFAR-10 classification and the explicit MNIST, SVHN and cross-corpus OOD comparisons disappear. Most original training datasets remain, including CIFAR-10 for image generation; replacing VAE with diffusion does not itself establish new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The new jailbreak experiments compare a Prompt control with Prompt + RS(split0) and Prompt + RS(split1), including attacks evaluated on their originating and paired models (Tables 8–10 and 12–14). These are localized comparator additions; the original overlap-method comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds pretrained ResNet/ViT finetuning at 224×224 resolution, LoRA finetuning of Llama models and diffusion UNet training, replacing the VAE setting. Reported scratch ResNet training changes to 50 epochs, and nanoGPT learning rate changes from 0.001 to 0.0005. New attack protocols specify three-step MI-FGSM with split-dependent perturbation budgets, 50 AdvBench requests, ASR and two LLM judges. Table 3 additionally uses CKNNA for diffusion.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Appendices A.3–A.4 add overlap-dependent transfer-robustness tests, white-box attack checks, assessments with two jailbreak judges, and successful/unsuccessful attack examples. The explicit distribution-shift analyses in v1 are removed. The seven-metric comparisons and t-SNE visualization remain, although their coverage and accompanying discussion change.

E5.justification: v1 specifies 10 seeds for image experiments and six for text; v2 specifies four per setting, with four-seed reporting also in Table 5 and the jailbreak tables. Means, standard deviations and plots showing seed variability already existed in v1. This changes reported replication counts without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation framework.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes from 0.360/0.566/0.747 to 0.584/0.771/0.891 for dataset/task/joint overlap, retaining the ranking. The model mix and diffusion metric differ, so these are revised aggregate results rather than comparable performance gains. v2 adds finetuned-model accuracies, diffusion FID results and extensive attack results: image-transfer ASR generally increases with overlap, whereas jailbreak-transfer ASR is largely flat. VAE and explicit OOD result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The training objective in Equation 1, representation/kernel definitions and mathematical overlap construction are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2's added experiments introduce no substantive theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: v2 retains the overlap–similarity and strongest-joint-overlap claims but adds a central contribution asserting increased vulnerability to transferable adversarial and jailbreak attacks. The title and abstract expand the paper from causes to consequences. The abstract also strengthens its original positive-correlation statement to causal language.

C2.justification: v2 interprets similarity as a security-risk indicator and attributes weak Llama trends to limited LoRA updates and finetuning data. It drops v1's VAE-capacity and ID/OOD explanations, the t-SNE explanation of decreasing CKA, and the warning that task-only comparisons use a different dataset. Figure 8 adds an explanation of diffusion FID differences through class coverage; the general limitations section is largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1.1 adds pretrained-model sources, model sizes, nanoGPT architecture, LoRA configuration and token budget, and UNet implementation details. Appendices A.3–A.4 document attack settings and evaluation samples. Conversely, v1's detailed hyperparameter matrix and GPU/FFCV disclosures disappear. Code and dataset access destinations change from GitHub/Kaggle to an anonymous repository/Google Drive.

R1.justification: v2 substantially extends positioning toward security consequences, adding transfer-attack and jailbreak literature such as Demontis et al., Dong et al., Andriushchenko et al. and Chao et al. Section 6 claims a previously unexplored connection between similarity and attack transfer. The earlier ensemble/multi-agent diversity motivation is removed; much of the representation-alignment literature remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are rewritten around causes and consequences. Separate overlap-method subsections are merged, implementation material moves into Appendix A.1, and the results narrative is refocused. The appendix is reorganized by training regime and gains dedicated attack sections, constituting substantial restructuring beyond added results alone.

P2.justification: Figures 4–6 are redesigned around architectures and model sizes instead of ID/OOD panels, and appendix metric grids are extensively rearranged. New attack plots, highlighted transfer-result tables and case-study tables are added. Table 5 expands into four model-specific blocks. The retained t-SNE plot is relocated, and the document adopts a different typesetting template.

improvement.justification: The expanded model experiments and diffusion checks strengthen empirical coverage, while the image-transfer study adds evidence of a practical consequence. However, v2 removes explicit OOD evaluations, reports fewer seeds, and promotes a central jailbreak-vulnerability claim despite nearly flat overlap–ASR relationships in Figures 7(a) and 23 and substantial judge disagreement in Appendix A.4. These are material gains in evidence alongside losses in robustness coverage and claim calibration; the PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
